item.title: Patrick Mackay And The Mystery Of His Unsolved Cases
item.description: Patrick Mackay was convicted in 1975 of three counts of manslaughter and sentenced to life imprisonment. Investigators also connected him to other deaths, although those cases were never proven in court. More than five decades later, Mackay remains in prison after his latest parole bid was refused in July 2026.

item.title: The Unexpected Person Behind Leslie Preer’s Death
item.description: TLeslie Preer was found dead inside her Chevy Chase, Maryland, home in May 2001, beginning a case that remained unsolved for more than two decades. In 2024, genetic genealogy led investigators to Eugene Gligor, her daughter’s former boyfriend. He later pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 22 years in prison.

item.title: The Mother Who Killed Her Two Children And Hid Them In A Freezer
item.description: When an eviction crew entered Mitchelle Blair's Detroit home in 2015, they discovered the bodies of her two children, Stoni Blair and Stephen Berry, inside a freezer. Blair later pleaded guilty to their murders and was sentenced to life without parole, claiming she believed the children had abused a younger sibling.

item.title: Richard Speck And The Night That Shocked Chicago
item.description: On July 13, 1966, Richard Speck broke into a Chicago townhouse where student nurses lived and murdered eight women over several hours. One nurse, Corazon Amurao, survived by hiding under a bed and later identified Speck in court. He was convicted of all eight murders and died in prison in 1991.

item.title: Her Ex Hid In The Crawl Space And Tried To Kill Her
item.description: Eilish Poe's ex-boyfriend, Jonathan Crossley, broke into her Colorado home and hid in the crawl space for more than 24 hours before attacking her. He stabbed Poe 16 times, but she survived by pretending to be dead until he fled. Crossley later died by suicide.

item.title: She Fell From A Cliff But The Evidence Told A Different Story
item.description: Deana Wild's 1987 death was initially ruled an accident after she fell from a Big Sur cliff. But a life insurance policy taken out just one day before her death, toxicology findings, and evidence from the scene led investigators to Virginia McGinnis. McGinnis was ultimately convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life without parole.

item.title: She Claimed She Remembered Her Father Killing Her Friend
item.description: Eileen Franklin-Lipsker said a childhood memory suddenly returned in 1989, leading her to accuse her father, George Franklin, of murdering her eight-year-old friend Susan Nason in 1969. Franklin was convicted and sentenced to life, but the conviction was overturned in 1995 and prosecutors dropped the case the following year, leaving the truth of the recovered memory deeply contested.
